extracted.intended_audience: Wikipedia readers and editors interested in disinformation, researchers and journalists seeking a compiled list of suspected troll-farm-linked websites
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia list article that compiles websites alleged by journalists and researchers to spread false information or impersonate news sites and that are likely linked to troll farms. Entries are grouped by country and presented in a tabular form with source citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criterion — described by journalists/researchers as spreading false information or impersonating news websites
rubrics_metrics.description: The following is a list of websites, separated by country, that have been described by journalists and researchers as spreading false information or impersonating news websites, and likely being linked to troll farms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should be those specifically identified in reliable secondary sources (journalistic investigations, academic research) as spreading false information or impersonating news outlets and plausibly connected to troll-farm operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization by country
rubrics_metrics.description: Websites in the list are separated by country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group entries under the country most relevant to the operation or attribution reported in sources; ensure the country grouping reflects the attribution in reliable sources rather than speculative association.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required table fields for each entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Table columns used on the page: Name; Domain; Status; Notes; Sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each listed site should include its name and domain, a status note (e.g., 'Impostor site affiliated with the Internet Research Agency'), explanatory notes summarizing the allegation or activity, and one or more source citations supporting the inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing and reliability / dynamic-list caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: This article contains dynamic lists that may never be able to satisfy particular standards for completeness. You can help by editing the page to add missing items, with references to reliable sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer high-quality, verifiable sources (investigative journalism, research reports, official documents). Avoid unsourced or poorly sourced claims; acknowledge the list's incompleteness and update entries when better attribution or refutation appears in reliable sources.
